title: Bunny runtime model artifact manifest
description: The contract at the trust boundary between Bunny Model Studio, which trains outside the image, and the Bunny OS runtime, which may load what it produced. A manifest describes an adapter and binds it by digest to the base model, dataset, configuration and commit that produced it; it does not confer anything. The 'permissions' array is present and must be empty: a model artifact cannot carry capabilities, and the field exists so that one attempting to is refused loudly instead of being ignored as an unknown key. Every section is closed - an unknown field is a refusal, matching capsules/manifest.py and catalog/entry.py - because a manifest is read across a trust boundary and a reader that ignores what it does not understand is a reader that can be talked past.

schemaVersion.description: The artifact format version. A version this build does not know is refused, never loaded.

modelId.description: The identifier the runtime registry uses. A single path segment: no separators, no leading dot, so a model id can never widen into a path.

adapterType.description: What kind of adapter this is. Only 'lora' is supported by this build; anything else is refused rather than attempted.

adapterFormat.description: The on-disk encoding. 'gguf' is what a llama.cpp backend can apply; 'peft-safetensors' is what Model Studio produces and no shipped backend can apply, so an artifact declaring it is validated but not activatable here.

adapterFile.description: The adapter's file name inside the artifact directory. A file name, never a path - the same rule the agent runtime applies to model files.

baseModel.description: What this adapter modifies. Compatibility is checked against this object as a whole: an adapter applied to the wrong base is not a degraded model, it is a different one.

revision.description: The exact revision the adapter was trained against. When this is absent, or is a moving name rather than a commit, compatibility cannot be established and validation reports UNKNOWN rather than passing.

file.description: The base weights' file name in a trusted model directory, when the runtime is expected to find them locally. A file name, never a path.

sha256.description: Digest of the local base weights, when known. Absent means base identity can be checked by name only, which is an UNKNOWN, not a PASS.

training.description: Provenance carried across the boundary. None of it is trusted as authority; all of it is recorded so a loaded model can be traced to what produced it.

intendedRuntime.description: Which Bunny runtime this artifact is for. An artifact intended for something else is refused rather than tried.

networkRequired.description: Always false. An artifact that declares it needs the network is refused: model loading does not introduce network access, and an artifact is not the place that decision gets made.

permissions.description: Always empty. A model artifact cannot carry, request or imply an operating-system capability. The field exists so that an artifact attempting to grant one is refused with a named code rather than silently ignored. Authority comes from the trust layer, the capability system and the user - never from a file that shipped with weights.
